    Propensity-weighted marginal effects with optional bootstrap

    Source: R/causal-ipw-bootstrap.R
    epi_ipw.Rd

    Fits a logistic propensity model for a binary exposure and computes separately normalized (Hájek) inverse-probability-weighted outcome risks, their difference and their ratio for the average-treatment-effect target population. Stabilized weights use the sample marginal exposure probabilities; group normalization means stabilized and unstabilized weights yield the same point risks. The returned propensity range, maximum weight and group effective sample sizes are descriptive diagnostics, not evidence that overlap or balance is adequate.

    Usage

    epi_ipw(
  .data,
  exposure,
  outcome,
  adjust = c(),
  stabilized = TRUE,
  bootstrap = 0L,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped data frame of independent individuals.

    exposure

    Binary 0/1 exposure column.

    outcome

    Binary 0/1 outcome column.

    adjust

    Tidy selection of complete baseline numeric, factor or logical covariates; defaults to an intercept-only exposure model.

    stabilized

    Whether to use stabilized ATE weights.

    bootstrap

    Number of individual bootstrap resamples, either 0 or an integer between 100 and 2000.

    conf_level

    Confidence level strictly between zero and one.

    Value

    A four-row tibble of weighted risks, risk difference and risk ratio, with percentile limits (missing without bootstrap), group effective sample sizes, propensity range, maximum weight and bootstrap counts.

    Details

    With bootstrap > 0, individual records are resampled, the propensity model is refit, and weights and contrasts are recalculated in every replicate. Intervals are percentile intervals; no cluster or survey-design bootstrap is included. Warned or failed bootstrap fits are omitted; more than 10 percent failures abort the analysis. Intervals conditional on successful fits can still be biased. Set a seed for reproducibility. Uncertainty from model selection or unmeasured confounding is not included.

    Causal interpretation requires consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, correct exposure-model specification, pre-exposure covariates, independent observations and appropriate censoring and missingness assumptions. These assumptions cannot be verified here. No weight trimming, missing-data handling, interactions, nonlinear terms or longitudinal treatment is provided. Use epi_balance() and substantive knowledge to assess the design.

    Examples

    d <- expand.grid(e = 0:1, age = 20:24, rep = 1:6)
d$y <- as.integer(d$rep <= 1 + d$e + (d$age %% 2))
epi_ipw(d, e, y, adjust = age)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 12
#>   measure         estimate conf_low conf_high     n ess_unexposed ess_exposed
#>   <chr>              <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <int>         <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 risk_unexposed     0.233       NA        NA    60            30          30
#> 2 risk_exposed       0.4         NA        NA    60            30          30
#> 3 risk_difference    0.167       NA        NA    60            30          30
#> 4 risk_ratio         1.71        NA        NA    60            30          30
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: propensity_min <dbl>, propensity_max <dbl>,
#> #   max_weight <dbl>, bootstrap <int>, bootstrap_success <int>
